topProblems.problem: The product pages are entirely vertical. The client's first ask (horizontal) is not met at any size.
topProblems.evidence: At ≥1024px it is a sticky right-hand card with 8 beats of 100svh scrolling vertically on the left. Below 1024px it is a plain vertical stack. Every route and viewport has 0px of horizontal travel. The story body takes 8.0-8.5 viewports of vertical scroll (4,840px at 1366x657), and the whole document is 9.8-11.3 viewports tall on desktop and 10.5 on a phone.
topProblems.rootCause: Story.tsx is built as vertical scrollytelling. `.beats` is normal flow of `.beat {min-height:100svh}`, `.stage` is `position:sticky; margin-bottom:-100svh`, and the only scroll logic is a ScrollTrigger that picks the beat whose midpoint is nearest the viewport centre and sets `active`. Nothing translates on the x axis.
topProblems.fix: Replace the stage and beats with a pinned horizontal scene track. Make `.story-track` a flex row of `.scene` panels, each 100vw wide and `calc(100svh - var(--header-h))` tall. Pin it with ScrollTrigger (`pin:true, scrub:0.6, end:()=>'+='+(track.scrollWidth-innerWidth), invalidateOnRefresh:true`), drive it with `gsap.to(track,{x:()=>-(track.scrollWidth-innerWidth),ease:'none'})`, and snap to panels (`snap:{snapTo:1/(n-1),duration:{min:.3,max:.6},ease:'power2.inOut'}`). Turn the rail into a bottom progress bar with labelled chapter links that jump via ScrollToPlugin to `st.start + i/(n-1)*(st.end-st.start)`. On touch devices or heights under ~560px, use a native horizontal scroll-snap rail instead of a pin (`overflow-x:auto; scroll-snap-type:x mandatory`, panels ~88vw) with prev/next buttons. Under reduced motion, show the same panels as a static complete list with no pin.
topProblems.files: components/story/Story.tsx, app/story.css, lib/breakpoints.ts (MQ for the horizontal pin, mirroring MQ.pinned but with a lower min-height)

topProblems.problem: There is no perceptible 3D depth, and no real background, midground and foreground planes.
topProblems.evidence: Measured at 1366x657 over the full 4,840px story: the lattice (.stage-bg) moves from -34 to +39px (73px), the visual layer (.stage-grid) from -48 to +55px (103px), and the text moves 4,840px. The two 'depth' layers differ by 30px across the whole page, about 0.6% of scroll. On screen it reads as a fixed card with text scrolling past it. Every visual sits in the same flat chrome (ink-950 card, 1px line, same radius, same shadow, same position).
topProblems.rootCause: Story.tsx sets BG_RATE=0.14 and MID_RATE=0.2 times `innerHeight*0.5`, spread over the entire story body. There is no perspective, no translateZ, and no per-scene layers. The foreground is just document flow.
topProblems.fix: Give each scene explicit planes moving at different horizontal rates via `containerAnimation`. (1) A back plate: a full-bleed product-tinted gradient, an oversized lattice, and a huge outlined chapter numeral or keyword, at about 0.3x track speed. (2) A midground: the diagram or real screen at 1x, inside `perspective:1200px`, easing from `rotateY(-10deg) translateZ(-80px)` to flat as it centres. (3) A foreground: the text card plus 2-3 floating callout chips built from the beat's own data (the 'Wait'/'Loop' warn nodes, a timecode like '00:14:32', a KPI from the real screen) at 1.25-1.4x with `translateZ(60px)` and a soft shadow. Animate transform and opacity only, and show the final state under reduced motion.

topProblems.problem: No scene has its own cinematic animation. The whole page uses one 12px crossfade.
topProblems.evidence: story.css has zero @keyframes. Its only transitions are `.stage-visual` opacity plus translateY(12px) and the rail ticks. The page's only other motion is the one-shot hero lattice assemble. All diagrams (split, lanes, flow, steps, tiles, wall, layers, records) are static DOM. Yisbir's 'One frame, four layers' is a flat stack where only 'PEOPLE' is legible, which hides 3 of the 4 layers the copy promises. The 'wall' is six identical striped boxes that read as broken placeholders.
topProblems.rootCause: BeatVisual.tsx renders static markup, and Story.tsx has no per-beat timeline: it only toggles `.is-active`.
topProblems.fix: Write one timeline per viz kind, triggered as its panel enters (`containerAnimation: trackTween, start:'left 75%', end:'center center', scrub`). Split: the 'as it runs' nodes build in sequence and the warn nodes nudge out of line. Lanes: the SVG case path draws across the departments (stroke-dashoffset). Flow: the edges draw and a dash runs back along the rework loop. Steps: an animated pipeline lights each step in turn. Layers: an exploded isometric stack (`rotateX(55deg) rotateZ(-30deg)`, layers separating along translateZ, each label fading in), which turns Yisbir's message into literal foreground/background. Wall: tiles power on, a scan line sweeps, one tile highlights with a timecode. Records: the query types in and rows stagger in. Real screens: a scale 1.08→1 plus clip-path reveal with chips pinned to real UI regions. Under reduced motion each scene renders its end state.

topProblems.problem: Beat 06 (features) renders nothing on all six product pages, and its six features never appear anywhere.
topProblems.evidence: Screenshots tasree3_1366x657_6-beat06.png and yisbir_1366x657_6-beat06.png show an empty right half. metricsAt recorded `.stage-visual.is-active` with no child (height 0), and the first audit run crashed on it. Below 1024px the beat is just a heading and one line.
topProblems.rootCause: In content/storyboards.ts, the features beats at lines 201, 328, 452, 590, 722 and 846 have `viz:{kind:'grid'}` but no `provenance`. BeatVisual.tsx calls `fail('draws a diagram but has no provenance')`, which returns null when NODE_ENV is production, so `next build` never throws. BeatText also skips `beat.features` when `viz.kind==='grid'`. The result: the features render neither as a visual nor as text.
topProblems.fix: Render the features list without a provenance gate, since it is a list rather than a diagram, or add `provenance:'Illustrative diagram'`. Also add a content unit test, run in CI rather than relying on the dev-only throw, that asserts every non-screen viz has provenance and every grid or steps viz has data.

topProblems.problem: The content is thin and repetitive: one template eight times, with the visuals restating the text.
topProblems.evidence: The whole page has ~450 words (tasree3 452, yisbir 432). Beat text runs 16-33 words except the walkthrough (78-82). There are only 2 real product images per page, and no next or previous product link (only 'All six products' pointing to /#products). The walkthrough visual repeats the step list beside it word for word, and its 5 steps wrap 4+1, orphaning the last one. Tile visuals restate headings: Tasree3 beat 8's tiles equal its features, and 3 tiles sit in a 2-column grid with an empty cell. Every beat is eyebrow, H2, 1-2 lines and a card on the right, with the same card size and position.
topProblems.rootCause: The storyboard schema gives each beat one short body and one viz, and Story.tsx renders all beats through one layout. Media already in content/media.ts (SCREENS.yisbirAlerts, SCREENS.yisbirPpeWall) is used only on the homepage scenario.
topProblems.fix: Vary the scene layouts: full-bleed screen, split diagram, centred statement, 6-card capability grid, and a closing panel. Give each scene a detail row of 2-3 chips taken from data already in the beat (warn nodes, timecodes, real-screen KPIs labelled 'demo data'). Add the existing register-backed screens (yisbirAlerts and yisbirPpeWall on Yisbir). Turn the walkthrough visual into an animated pipeline instead of a duplicate list. End with a 'next product' panel that shows the next product's real screen. Do not invent claims: any new line must come from register items marked ok-to-use or use-with-edit.

topProblems.problem: Layout breaks at short laptop heights (1536x730, 1366x657, 1280x601) and at 1024x768.
topProblems.evidence: The hero CTA is below or on the fold at 1536x730 (bottom at 730/763), 1366x657 (730/763) and 1280x601 (722/754). The hero is 1.1-1.37 viewports tall and the H1 is always 4 lines at 66-68px. Beat 1's 514px split card slides under the 73px fixed header (top at y=53 at 1536x730, 23 at 1366x657, 0 at 1280x601, 68 at 1024x768), which hides the 'As drawn / As it runs' labels. The walkthrough beat is 1.19-1.49 viewports tall, so its text is clipped while the card stays still. The chapter-rail ticks overlap the card's right edge at 1280 and 1024 widths.
topProblems.rootCause: `.story-hero` uses padding-block 148px 72px and an H1 clamp up to 4.25rem in a 6/12 column. `.stage` is a full 100svh that includes the header area, `.stage-mid` centres the visual with no max-height, and the parallax adds about -48px. `.beat` has no height budget. `.stage-rail` sits at `right: gutter/2` inside the content area.
topProblems.fix: Hero: `padding-top: calc(var(--header-h) + clamp(16px,4svh,48px))`, `font-size: min(clamp(2.5rem,1.4rem+3.4vw,4.25rem), 9svh)`, a 7/12 text column, and an `@media (max-height:760px)` compaction (smaller sub, name moment inline) so the CTA fits in the first viewport from 600px tall up. Scenes: height `calc(100svh - var(--header-h))` below the header, and visuals capped at `max-height: calc(100svh - var(--header-h) - 2*var(--sp-6))` with screens scaled to fit. Size type with `min(vw, svh)` clamps. Move the rail into a bottom progress bar outside the content columns.

topProblems.problem: Scrolling between beats is dead air, and the text and visual go out of sync.
topProblems.evidence: In the between-beat screenshots, about half of each frame is empty: the previous body is leaving at the top and the next heading entering at the bottom, while the card has already switched (1920x937 tasree3 shows beat 3's tiles beside beat 2's text, and yisbir 1280x601 shows the layers card beside beat 2's text). At 1920x937 and 1440x900, 30-38% of scroll positions have under 25% text coverage, and at 768x1024 it is 47%. On wide screens the visual takes 9-17% of the viewport and the text 5-6%.
topProblems.rootCause: Each beat is 100svh with short, centred text, and the active visual is chosen by nearest midpoint, so it switches about half a viewport before the matching text is readable. The ~1184px container leaves ~370px empty on each side at 1920px.
topProblems.fix: In the horizontal track, each scene's text and visual live in one panel and arrive together, and snapping ensures the user never rests between scenes. Use a full-bleed back plate and let the visual grow to about 55-60vw at ≥1440px, so a 1920px frame is composed rather than mostly empty.

topProblems.problem: The ending is broken and abrupt, and the hero leaks the stage.
topProblems.evidence: At 1366x657 and 1280x601, the close's solid top edge slices Yisbir's beat 8 PPE screen in half (y≈230). At 1920x937 a ~250px empty lattice band sits above the Tasree3 close. On a phone the close is preceded by a sliced screen tail and a ~200px empty band. At 1920x937, beat 1's dark card peeks over the bottom of the hero (y=920). The close itself is a text-only band with the right half empty.
topProblems.rootCause: The sticky stage, with `margin-bottom:-100svh` and `.story-body{overflow:clip}`, keeps the last visual on screen until `.story-close` (z-index 3, solid background) covers it. The stage begins immediately under the hero.
topProblems.fix: Make the close the last panel inside the pinned track (product CTA, 'All six products', and a next-product teaser with its real screen), so the pin releases only after the ending is fully composed. Start the track below the hero with its own entrance so nothing peeks.

topProblems.problem: Phones and tablets get the weakest version: a long vertical stack with duplicated content and no swipe.
topProblems.evidence: 390x844 runs 10.5 screens, and the walkthrough beat is 1.62-1.67 screens tall because the step list is followed by the same steps as a diagram. 768x1024 runs 7.9-8 viewports, with 31-47% of positions mostly empty. Yisbir's layers visual is an empty frame reading 'PEOPLE'. Beat 06 shows no features.
topProblems.rootCause: Story.tsx never loads GSAP below 1024px and falls back to inline vertical beats. The CSS duplicates content (beat-steps plus a viz-steps diagram).
topProblems.fix: Below 1024px, or on any touch device, use a native horizontal scroll-snap scene rail (no pin, no GSAP needed). Each card holds the visual on top and the text below and fits within `100svh - header`. Add a progress or dot indicator and prev/next buttons that are visibly focusable. Run lightweight per-card reveal animations from an IntersectionObserver on the rail root. Drop the duplicated steps diagram. Reduced motion keeps the same rail, static and complete.
